question: Which of the following types of engine classifications is based on the thermodynamic cycle?
solution:
The correct answer is __Otto cycle engine.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Otto cycle engine__ is based on the thermodynamic cycle.
 
• The Otto cycle describes the thermodynamic principles behind internal combustion engines used in most modern automobiles.
 
• The cycle involves four distinct processes: intake, compression, power (combustion), and exhaust.
 
• Engines operating on the Otto cycle are typically spark-ignition engines.
 
• The efficiency of the Otto cycle depends on the compression ratio of the engine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Radial Engine:**

 
 
• A radial engine is a type of internal combustion engine with cylinders arranged in a circular pattern around the crankshaft.
 
• It is commonly used in aircraft engines.
 
 
 
• **V-engine:**
 
 
• V-engine is characterized by cylinders arranged in a V-shaped configuration.
 
• It is designed to save space and reduce engine size.
 
 
 
• **In-line Cylinder Engine:**
 
 
• In-line cylinder engines have cylinders arranged in a straight line.
 
• They are commonly used in smaller vehicles.
